newsitem.title: USA: Salomon cuts Chrysler Q2 EPS estimate.
newsitem.headline: Salomon cuts Chrysler Q2 EPS estimate.

text.p: - Salomon Brothers auto analyst John Kirnan said he is reducing his estimate for Chrysler Corp.'s second quarter net income to $0.70 a share from $0.90 previously because of disappointing May sales results and increasing incentive costs.

-- Kirnan said in a research report that the downward revision, his third for Chrysler this year, brings his full-year 1997 estimate for Chrysler to $4.05 a share. The revision reflects an increase in Chrysler's estimated incentive costs to $975 per vehicle from $900.

-- Kirnan said there is underlying weakness in the minivan market, reflected by Chrysler's 6.2 percent decline in minivan sales for May versus a year earlier, despite increasing incentives to up to $1,000 on the vehicles. Sales of Dodge's regular-cab Ram pickup truck were also down 50 percent, despite healthy inventories of 92 days at the end of May.

-- Sales of Chrysler's Jeep Grand Cherokee sport utility vehicle fell 16.4 percent, but Kirnan attributed the drop less to an engine plant strike and more to competition from newer sport utility entries.

-- Kirnan said downside risk in the shares is minimal, given the company's attractive dividend yield of 4.9 percent, its continuation of a $2 billion share repurchase program for 1997 and new model introductions later this year.

"Although the shares remain rated a strong Hold, we would not be surprised to see the shares broach its all-time high of $37 per share by year-end, particularly if Fed policy remains on hold and the dollar/yen exchange rate remains on hold," Kirnan wrote.
-- Chrysler shares were unchanged at 32-1/8 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
